assumptions: The definition covers the whole movement as one repetition: the clean from the floor, then the split jerk to overhead lockout.
Bilateral laterality: both arms and both legs perform the same actions. The split-stance foot placement in the jerk is not modeled as one-sided loading.
Joint actions describe the exertion phases: the pulls and the recovery drive, the third-pull shrug and elbow flexion, and the jerk drive and overhead lockout.
Calf plantarflexion, elbow flexion in the third pull and upward scapular rotation overhead only accompany the lift, so they are marked assist.
Scapular elevation (the shrug) is treated as a primary action of the third pull.
Trunk extension is not listed as an action because the instructions say to hold the back angle, so the spinal erectors are credited through anti_flexion_spine.
The load is held in the hands during the pull and on the front shoulders in the rack, so grip, wrist_stability and shoulder_position_hold are all included.
Heavy bracing is assumed for a loaded expert-level lift.
Edited by the council from revision 99d95fbe8a97, as the reviewer proposed: add demand glenohumeral_stabilization.
classification_reasons: The catalog name and the numbered instructions describe a full clean followed by a split jerk with a barbell, which the tracer can represent with the olympic_lift family and its joint actions and demands.
The contact sheet shows the clean setup (bar at the shins, overhand grip, hips low) and the front-squat rack position, and this matches instruction steps 1 to 5.
Both frames are consistent with the text. Neither frame shows the jerk, so the jerk is taken from the written instructions only.
